frontispiece.note: frontispiece etching in the Leviathan's four registers -- blank banner, the colossus between pilasters, ten framed vignettes in two columns, blank plinth. The body is an open clockwork movement worked over with engraved circuit tracery, gold in the trim of every detail; the colossus of clerks it replaces is retired. Style reference: the retired plate, for etching craft only. Best of six candidates.
frontispiece.prompt:
FULL BLEED: the etching fills the image edge to edge to edge to edge. No plate mark, no border
rule, no surrounding sheet, no blank margin on any side.

Reference image 1 is the STYLE TEMPLATE for craft only: match its seventeenth-century copper-plate
etching technique, its aged laid paper -- warm, toned, lightly foxed, the ink slightly uneven as a
worn plate prints -- its dense burin cross-hatching and fine stipple, its baroque frontispiece
character. The line is a single dark brown-black ink, and burnished GOLD LEAF picks out the trim of
every detail: the fillets and ruled borders of each compartment, the ornament of the banner, the
capitals and bases of the pilasters, the bezels and rims of the machinery, the highlights on metal.
The gold is trim and highlight only, never a fill.

COMPOSITION, after the frontispiece of Hobbes's Leviathan, in four registers stacked down the page:

TOP REGISTER: a wide ornamental banner spanning the full width, its interior a completely blank,
smooth, empty panel. Nothing is written in it.

UPPER REGISTER, the largest: a colossal allegorical figure rising from the sea, filling the centre,
its body an armoured mechanism -- NOT made of people. Its torso is an open clockwork movement of
toothed gears, escapements, mainspring barrels and jewelled bearings, and over and through that
movement runs extremely fine engraved circuit tracery, the etched lines of a printed circuit board
rendered in burin hatching, with gold on every gear rim, bezel and trace. Its head is a calm helm of
concentric rings around a single lens. In its
right hand it holds a surveyor's staff upright; in its left, an unrolled scroll whose surface is
blank. Behind it a lighthouse on a rock and a working harbour of stone quays. Flanking the figure,
one tall stone pilaster at the far left and one at the far right, each carrying a narrow vertical
blank panel down its shaft -- smooth and empty, no writing.

LOWER REGISTER: two symmetrical columns of small framed vignettes, five stacked down the left edge
and five down the right edge, each in its own thin ruled compartment, each a separate little
engraved still life in the same ink: a single open ledger with one pen laid across it and a
gilt fillet round its board; a lighthouse seen close; an anchor with a coil of chain; a heavy
strongroom door with one slot; a pair of balance scales; a mariner's compass rose with a gilt limb;
a bonded chest with a broken seal; a fleet of small boats seen from above; an escapement and
train of gears drawn as a horologist would draw them; a bridge of one span between two shores.

BASE REGISTER: a low plinth running the full width, its face a blank empty panel.

Absolutely no lettering, numerals, words, letterforms, inscriptions, signatures or symbols that
resemble writing anywhere in the image. Every banner, panel, scroll, pilaster and plinth face is
left smooth and completely empty; the lettering is typeset afterwards.
frontispiece.style_reference: the previous frontispiece.jpg (craft only: etching technique, paper, hatching)
frontispiece.chosen_rationale: the only candidate where the torso reads as a real movement -- gears, escapement and circuit tracery together -- with all four registers intact and every type area left empty

frontispieces.why: The Leviathan brief measured against the plate already in the book: the cyclopean lens emitted nothing, the scroll was blank rather than a Float Plan of hashes, there was no subterranean Merkle-and-gearing cutaway, the sceptre was a plain staff, and the colossus waded in the harbour instead of towering over it. One plate also served all three editions, so the etching faced the Swiss edition's flat colour blocks.

plates.plates/frontispiece.jpg: maritime, watercolour, variant w3. The first pass was a sepia intaglio engraving, which is the TECHNICAL edition's register -- the maritime plates are faded watercolour washes, so the frontispiece was out of family with the book it opens. Redrawn as a wash: a benign colossus at the water whose body is a swarm of small robots, one hand beckoning open-palmed rather than commanding, holding Hobbes's sword and crozier translated as a braided ethernet trunk and a fibre-optic crook. Copper commands, glass attests.
